previous_action: Gaius Maximus Valerius organizes all the armed men under his command, trains them personally, and spends a full day with them to demonstrate leadership and virtue.

continuity.campaign_development: In March 60 BCE, Valerius brought all armed men serving across his estates, roads, lake port and Roman household under a common training order. He personally drilled with them and spent a full day sharing their duties, while field exercises tested the coordination of infantry, cavalry, guards and supply handlers. The result was a more unified pattern of service across a force that remained distributed among several holdings.
